To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• There are differences between participants in terms of how they respond to their deliberative experience.

(a) the most politically engaged participants were more likely to change their opinion on a number of policy issues; (b) those with higher levels of political knowledge were more likely to shift their opinions; and (c) the most engaged and knowledgeable citizens were the most likely to feel they had benefitted from the deliberative process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: To what extent do the capacities of the citizens involved in deliberation influence the outcomes of deliberation?

(1) the extent to which deliberative democracy is capable of changing people’s opinions; (2) whether the extent to which people change their opinions is dependent on their prior level of political knowledge; and (3) whether there are systematic biases in the way deliberation works.
the following question: Are some people better able to benefit from deliberation, and if so, why?
